subject: Event summary and commitments — Mar 18 service event
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@bluelinepayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Event summary and commitments — Mar 18 service event

Alex —

Thank you again for the patience yesterday while we worked through the service disruption that affected embedding requests for a subset of BlueLine customers. I wanted to share a concise summary of what happened, immediate mitigations we put in place, and concrete next steps we are committing to. We know this incident impacted your nightly batch runs and the reporting window — we are sorry for that disruption.

Summary (brief)
- What: Intermittent failures and elevated latency for the embedding endpoint between 06:45–09:20 PDT on 2027-03-18. A portion of requests experienced timeouts or partial responses.
- Impact: ~18% of embedding requests for BlueLine were delayed or errored; no data exfiltration detected.
- Root cause (short): A combination of a recently deployed kernel selection heuristic and a stale KV-cache invalidation sequence created a cascading retry storm on a small GPU pool, exhausting capacity.

Immediate mitigations taken
- Rolled back the heuristic and reverted to the previous kernel selection within 22 minutes of detection.
- Throttled background retry logic for that pool to prevent cascading retries.
- Provisioned temporary burst capacity for BlueLine traffic to clear backlog.

What you’ll find attached/linked
- A one-page postmortem summary (attached) with our timeline and action owners.
- Full event timeline CSV (attached).
- Internal ticket we opened tracking fixes and rollout plan (link below).

Committed next steps (what we will do and by when)
1) Stable rollback and canary: permanent fix to kernel-selection flow + staged canary across your production pool — target 2027-03-25. (Owner: Ben)
2) Safe retry behavior: implement exponential backoff caps and per-pool retry throttles — target 2027-03-29. (Owner: Dylan)
3) Capacity safeguards: automatic burst scaling threshold adjustments for Dedicated customers and an alert we will add specifically tuned to BlueLine traffic patterns — target 2027-04-01. (Owner: Stephanie)
4) Credit & follow-up: we will propose a service credit for the impact window and schedule a 1:1 to review the postmortem and any additional mitigation requests — propose slot next week.

If you’d like a short run-through on a call, we can do 20 minutes to walk the timeline and answer questions. Again, apologies — we’re making these changes a high priority.

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment stubs: redwood-postmortem-summary-20270320.pdf (summary, timeline, owners), service-timeline-20270318.csv (detailed event log)

Cc: BlueLine Ops <ops-manager@bluelinepayments.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Event summary and commitments — Mar 18 service event

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the quick summary and the attachments. A couple quick clarifying questions before we sync: 

1) Can you confirm whether batched nightly jobs that started at ~05:30 were retried by BlueLine systems or by Redwood? We saw some retries from our side but also a large number of late responses.
2) For the proposed credit — what is your standard approach for a Distributed Denial or service degradation window? We will need specifics for our finance team.

Would like to schedule the 1:1 to go through the timeline and any longer-term SLA guardrails. Morning PST next Tuesday (03/23) or Wednesday (03/24) works for our ops lead.

Best,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
BlueLine Payments

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: BlueLine — Detailed RCA and action plan (follow-up)

Alex —

Following up with the requested details and the longer RCA. I’ve pasted the executive timeline below and included our remediation plan and verification criteria. The attached PDF is the one-page summary we referenced; the CSV contains per-request traces.

Executive RCA (concise)- Trigger: On 2027-03-18 06:37:12 PDT, a new kernel-selection heuristic was rolled into the fleet to improve throughput for short-context models. The heuristic interacted poorly with a concurrent asynchronous KV-cache invalidation job, which briefly caused elevated miss rates.
- Effect: Elevated misses produced increased upstream latency; client SDKs and our gateway retried requests according to default retry behavior. On a small, already-congested GPU pool used by BlueLine we observed a retry amplification effect that saturated queue capacity and caused timeouts.
- Data access/exposure: No customer data left the cluster; all logs are access-controlled and we have not detected unauthorized exfiltration.

Timeline (high level)
- 06:37 PDT — Kernel selection heuristic deploy completed (canary -> fleet).
- 06:42 PDT — First elevated latency alerts observed by platform monitoring.
- 06:45–07:07 PDT — Retry rate spikes; retries amplify load on pool.
- 07:09 PDT — Automatic alert escalations to on-call; team begins mitigation.
- 07:20 PDT — Rolled back kernel heuristic and throttled retry logic; immediate latency improvements observed.
- 07:44 PDT — Temporary burst capacity provisioned to clear backlog.
- 09:20 PDT — Metrics returned to baseline; incident closed.

Remediation plan & verification (owners + dates)
1) Kernel-selection fix: adjust heuristic to respect per-pool load signals; unit/integration tests added + canary plan — Ben — complete by 2027-03-25. Verification: canary traffic shows no latency delta and unit tests included in CI.
2) Retry policy harden: add per-pool exponential backoff and overall retry caps; integrate into SDK defaults — Dylan — complete by 2027-03-29. Verification: synthetic workload demonstrates no retry amplification.
3) Capacity alerts: tune autoscaler thresholds and add anomaly alerts for per-customer retry amplification — Stephanie — complete by 2027-04-01. Verification: alert fires in synthetic test; runbook updated.
4) Post-deployment audit: 30-day audit of recent kernel changes with a focus on interactions with cache invalidations — Ben/Dylan — start 2027-03-22; report due 2027-04-20.

Service credit & next steps
- We propose a targeted service credit for the impacted window (2027-03-18 06:40–09:20 PDT). We’ll calculate the credit and send a proposal by EOD Monday (2027-03-22).
- Suggested 1:1 with your ops lead: Tue 03/23 10:00–10:30 PDT. If that works we’ll send a calendar invite and include the technical owners.

Links & artifacts
- Postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/blueline-2027-03-18
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4521 (tracking remediation)

We take this seriously and will keep you updated at the milestones above. If you’d like more instrumentation or a dedicated alerting rule for BlueLine before the fixes land, we can prioritize that work.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Thanks Stephanie and Ben — appreciate the thorough write-up and the suggested remediation schedule. The ops lead (cc’d) accepts the Tue 03/23 10:00 PDT slot; please include the owners you listed. Two quick asks before the call:
1) Please share the draft service credit calculation in the invite or ahead of the meeting so our finance team can review.
2) Can you add an alert to our account that triggers when retry rate for our customer_id > 3% for a sustained 5m window? If you can provision that before Tue we’ll test it live in our staging run Monday night.

Looking forward to the call.
